fields.description_1:
C10media works across outdoor media, digital, radio, television and print, so a client may arrive with a campaign goal rather than a preferred channel. Listing every medium at the same level would force visitors to design their own media plan before they understand where the agency can help. Project examples matter, but they need context to show the thinking behind them.

The website therefore needed to connect strategy, channels and work without turning the portfolio into a gallery of logos. Decision makers also needed a route to discuss a campaign after they had enough information. On mobile, media categories had to stay readable without long agency copy. The portfolio problem was to explain a multi-channel media service without inventing reach, campaign uplift or return-on-investment results.
fields.description_2:
I organised C10media around the campaign decision rather than around a long inventory of media products. Strategy gives the starting context, while outdoor, digital, radio, television and print can each explain where they fit. Project examples support those routes and show relevant work without being treated as proof of future campaign performance.

Contact actions appear after the visitor has enough context to describe an objective, audience or channel question. I kept headings concrete and the mobile hierarchy compact so media options remain easy to scan. The portfolio case now explains how WordPress brings planning, channel expertise and project work together in one agency experience, while avoiding unsupported claims about reach, conversion, awareness or commercial return that would require campaign-specific measurement.

fields.description_1:
Administratiegids helps entrepreneurs compare accounting providers, which means the site has to do more than publish company listings. A visitor may start with a location, service need or quote request. Provider information, reviews and local relevance must work together without suggesting that one listing is automatically the best choice.

The platform therefore needed a clear route from a financial need to suitable providers and then to a comparison or quote request. Guidance content had to support the decision without overwhelming pages. Mobile visitors also need forms and provider cards to remain easy to use. The portfolio story had to avoid invented savings, ranking claims or guarantees about provider quality. The challenge was to make comparison useful while keeping the platform neutral and understandable.
fields.description_2:
I structured Administratiegids around the steps an entrepreneur follows when looking for accounting support. Visitors can move from a service or location need to relevant provider profiles, review available information and then request quotes when they are ready to compare. Guidance stays close to the decision it helps explain instead of competing with the provider results.

Provider cards use consistent information so comparison is easier, while reviews remain supporting evidence rather than a guarantee of fit. On mobile, local results, forms and quote actions keep a predictable order. The portfolio case now describes a WordPress comparison platform with clear discovery and enquiry routes, without claiming that listed providers are universally better, that users always save money or that the site guarantees a financial outcome.

fields.description_1:
Miamicarwash is a local car-care service where visitors often want simple answers quickly: what services are available, where is the location and how can they get in touch? Strong visual branding can help the business stand out, but it can also push practical information below large images or promotional sections.

The website therefore needed to balance the car-wash identity with a straightforward service path. Customers should be able to understand the main care options and find location or contact details without exploring a large site. Mobile use is especially important for a local service people may check while travelling. The portfolio story had to focus on the real service experience without inventing wash quality, waiting times, customer satisfaction or visit growth that were not measured.
fields.description_2:
I built the Miamicarwash WordPress experience around immediate local-service questions. The main car-care options are introduced early, followed by practical information and clear location or contact actions. Visual content supports the energetic brand but does not replace the details someone needs before deciding to visit or make contact.

The page remains compact so users are not sent through unnecessary navigation for a simple local task. On mobile, service information, location details and actions stay prominent and easy to tap. The portfolio case now explains how the site combines a distinctive visual identity with a practical customer route, while avoiding unsupported claims about waiting time, cleaning results, customer satisfaction or traffic growth that would need separate operational evidence.

fields.description_1:
Taxicentralerijswijk serves passengers with transport needs, including local rides, airport journeys and business travel. An airport passenger needs flight-related clarity, while a local passenger may care about pickup, destination and quick contact. Treating every ride as the same service would make the booking path less useful.

The website therefore needed to separate ride types, keep practical travel information close to each route and make booking or contact easy from a phone. Pricing or availability should not be implied unless the service can support it. The portfolio case also had to avoid promises about arrival times or duration because traffic and operations change. The challenge was to make several taxi services understandable while keeping the next action simple for passengers who may be arranging travel quickly.
fields.description_2:
I organised Taxicentralerijswijk around the type of journey a passenger is planning. Local rides, airport transport and business travel have their own context, so visitors can understand what information belongs to the request before opening a booking or contact route. Practical travel details sit beside the service instead of being scattered across unrelated pages.

The mobile experience keeps ride choices, contact actions and essential information easy to reach for people arranging transport away from a desk. I used direct labels and avoided promises about exact pickup or journey times that depend on live conditions. The portfolio case now presents a focused taxi-service flow in WordPress, showing how different ride needs connect to a clear next step without claiming operational results that were not independently verified.

fields.description_1:
Vanbachfinance needs to explain financial support to businesses that may arrive with questions about administration, reporting, tax work or finance guidance. These topics are connected, but a visitor should not have to understand internal structure before finding the relevant service. Dense financial language would make that first step harder.

The website therefore needed a hierarchy that separates finance work from advisory support while keeping their relationship clear. Contact options had to follow useful information instead of becoming the only message. On mobile, service routes needed to remain readable without long blocks of terminology. The portfolio story also had to avoid promises about tax savings, profit or financial performance. The challenge was to make a professional finance offer understandable and evidence-led for business decision makers.
fields.description_2:
I structured Vanbachfinance around the financial tasks clients are likely to recognise first. Administration, reporting, tax support and finance guidance each receive a clear route, with supporting information added where it helps someone decide whether the service fits their question. Contact actions appear after that context so an enquiry can be specific.

The hierarchy keeps routine financial work easy to find without reducing broader advice to a vague consultancy message. I used plain headings and measured claims instead of promises about savings, compliance or business growth. On smaller screens, service cards and contact routes keep the same priority. The portfolio case now explains the actual WordPress information structure and decision path for a finance business without relying on repetitive agency wording or unverified financial outcomes.
